intended_object: The standard basis element of the Brauer algebra B_k(δ) over a commutative semiring R that corresponds to a Brauer diagram D on k strands, i.e. the diagram D viewed as an element of the algebra. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The library builds the Brauer algebra as a one-field structure around the coefficient function `BrauerDiagram k →₀ R`. The definition `of D` is `ofCoeff (Finsupp.single D 1)`: the element whose coefficient is 1 at D and 0 at every other diagram. This is exactly the basis vector for D in the free R-module on the diagrams. The library backs this up: `of_mul_of` proves the loop rule D₁·D₂ = δ^c (D₁∘D₂) on these elements, `one_def` shows the unit is `of` of the identity diagram, and `basis` is built from `coeffLinearEquiv`, so the basis vector it gives at D is `of D`. The setting (any commutative semiring R, any loop value δ, any k) is the natural generality for the Brauer algebra. Mathlib has no Brauer algebra; the closest analogue is `MonoidAlgebra.of`, but that is a different construction.
